analysis.title: Global Equity Presentation: Reassessing the Balance of Risks, Neutralizing Growth
key_insights: Citi tactically downgrades the US, Global Tech and European Tech to Neutral from Overweight. Fundamentals look attractive, but positioning is roughly neutral and could move into net short territory after the recent selloff.
Citi remains constructive on AI over the medium term. It wants cleaner positioning, more stable AI sentiment and steady EPS revisions before restoring Overweight on Tech.
Europe ex-UK is upgraded to Overweight from Neutral. The market is less sensitive to Tech and more levered to falling oil prices than peers. Europe Food & Bev is also upgraded to Overweight.
Global sector strategy is now a barbell of Cyclicals and Defensives, with Overweights in Materials and Health Care (Health Care upgraded from Neutral).

Before the recent selloff, global equities moved sideways while Defensives outperformed Cyclicals by as much as 15pp in a month in both the US and Europe. Citi says this 'steady market, violent rotation' pattern is rare and has historically occurred only in major stress episodes (2008, 2020, 2022).

Citi describes risks as balanced, not skewed to the downside. Positives: oil has fallen on easing geopolitical risk, bond yields and Fed pricing are off highs, and macro data is resilient. Negatives: credit spreads are wider, earnings revisions have slowed, and AI sentiment has fallen after the US midterms raised doubts about the AI buildout and capex.
Nasdaq positioning was roughly neutral at the prior close. Reaching -3 on Citi's normalised positioning scale (+5 max long, -5 max short) would take roughly another 5% price decline.

Consensus expects global EPS growth to slow by about 20pp in 2027E, from +37% in 2026E to +16%. Citi finds global stocks rose about 4% on average in 'positive but decelerating' EPS growth years, with rotation toward Defensives and Quality.

Tech is expected to deliver about half of global EPS growth in 2026E and about 70% in 2027E (about 80% in the US). That would be the second most concentrated positive-growth year on record. Citi finds little link between EPS concentration and overall market performance.

Index targets: S&P 500 8100 at end-2026 (+5% from 7689). Stoxx 600 640 (-3%) with a mid-2027 target of 700. Euro Stoxx 50 6400, FTSE 100 10700, Topix 4700 (+21%), MSCI EM 1870 (+20%), MSCI ACWI Local 1440 (+6%). Citi forecasts about 5% global upside to year-end, assuming geopolitical tensions keep easing.

Global 12m forward PE has derated by 23% in 2026. The US remains expensive (forward PE 19.1, CAPE 44.3) while the UK (12.0) and EM (8.9) are cheapest. Europe trades at a 25-30% discount to the US that has narrowed but remains large.

Citi's global Bear Market Checklist is at 10/18 red flags, the highest since the GFC. It does not yet signal 'overexuberance'. Once the count reaches double digits it has historically risen faster, and further flags would mean dips should not necessarily be bought.

Energy prices are more closely tied to 10Y US yields than at any point in 30 years, and their correlation with equities is the most negative in three decades. The path of the US-Iran conflict is therefore central to risk assets. Citi commodity strategists see European gas falling to the mid-50s EUR/MWh by year-end under various Strait of Hormuz reopening and weather scenarios.

The Fed has returned to rate hikes, two years after its first cut of the cycle. Historically, global equities wobble around the first hike but are up on average 6-12 months later. The US tends to underperform after the first hike, while Japan and Europe outperform and Value beats Growth by 3-5%.

French OAT spreads are now wider than Italian BTPs. Marine Le Pen is the polling front-runner for the April 2027 French presidential election, and French banks look potentially rich relative to spreads.

AI trade volatility is rising. Citi believes the market underestimates hyperscaler AI revenue growth. AI-linked HY spreads are back at their wides on Neocloud pressure, and USD hyperscaler IG issuance is roughly doubling from about $90bn in 2025 to about $180bn in 2026.
EM changes: Korea is neutralised on volatile trading, despite screening well in the allocation model. China is upgraded to Overweight and Mexico to Neutral as potential 'broadening' candidates.
Citi expects a policy pivot in China to become more likely in 2027, with the year-end Politburo and CEWC meetings giving the first clues.

European autonomy policy (procurement preferences, local content rules, trade defence) is further advanced than markets appreciate. Citi sees a possible 10% index re-rating to about 16x over the longer term, favouring Cyclicals, Value and SMID caps.

earnings_insights: Consensus global EPS growth for 2026E is +37% and for 2027E is +16% (consensus estimates, not reported figures). The deceleration of about 20pp is one of the largest in the sample since the mid-1980s.

Bottom-up 2026E EPS growth is +37% for global equities. Top-down forecasts for 2026E are strongest in the US and EM. Mag 8 EPS growth is +57% in 2026E against +23% for the other 492 S&P 500 stocks (consensus).
Stoxx 600 full-year 2026E EPS growth consensus is +21%, and Q3 2026 is expected at +26% y/y (consensus). Price reaction to European beats and misses has been muted and symmetrical so far.

European earnings revisions have been in net upgrade territory for 24 consecutive weeks. Revisions also bucked the usual pre-reporting-season weakness for the second straight quarter, which has happened only six times in 25 years.
Tech is expected to contribute about 70% of global EPS growth in 2027E (about 80% in the US), per consensus.
US S&P 500 index earnings of $365 underpin Citi's 2026 price target upside.

risk_factors: Positioning on Nasdaq and other key indices could reset into net short territory.
AI sentiment has fallen and AI-linked HY spreads are back at their wides on Neocloud pressure.
Earnings revisions have decelerated and global EPS growth is expected to slow by about 20pp in 2027E.
Tech concentration of EPS growth is rising, to about 70% of global growth in 2027E.
The Bear Market Checklist is at its highest since the GFC and above 10 flags has historically accelerated.
US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz developments affect energy prices and risk assets.
The Fed has returned to rate hikes, and long-end yields are rising.
French fiscal stress and the 2027 presidential election could widen OAT spreads further.
A higher USD would hurt EM and the relative performance of non-US equities.

Single stock volatility in the S&P 500 has been immense, and the Growth cluster beta and the weight of high-beta stocks in the index are rising.
Citi's Bear Market Checklist stands at 10/18 red flags, the highest since the GFC, though still below levels preceding past bear markets.
US investors cut holdings of European-only equity funds by about 30% of AUM from 2022 to 2025. Citi says the unwind of that trend has much further to go.
geopolitical: The path of the US-Iran conflict is cited as crucial for risk assets, and easing geopolitical risk has helped push oil lower.
The Strait of Hormuz reopening is a scenario variable in Citi commodity strategists' gas price forecast.
US midterm elections raised questions about the longer-term trajectory of the AI buildout and capex.
French fiscal and political concerns have pushed OAT spreads above Italian BTP spreads. Marine Le Pen is the front-runner for the April 2027 presidential election.
Europe is caught between a more protectionist US and an assertive China, with EU trade defence, steel regime and merger guideline changes in progress.
China policy pivot is possible in 2027, with year-end Politburo and CEWC meetings as first clues.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil has fallen on easing geopolitical risk, yields and Fed pricing are off highs, macro data is resilient, valuations have reset lower, and 2027E EPS forecasts are largely unchanged.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit spreads have risen, earnings revisions have slowed, AI sentiment has plunged after the US midterms, and the Bear Market Checklist is at 10/18, its highest since the GFC.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nasdaq positioning moving to -3 after another c5% decline, and further Bear Market Checklist flags turning on, would signal dips should not necessarily be bought.

tension_points.bull_case: Citi believes the market underestimates hyperscaler AI revenue growth, and consensus revisions after 3Q results were upward, with capex still growing.
tension_points.bear_case: AI sentiment is volatile, AI-linked HY spreads are back at their wides on Neocloud pressure, and data center bondholders rely on tenant credit that can reprice quickly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Citi wants cleaner positioning and more stable AI sentiment along with steady EPS revisions before restoring Overweight.
